headline: Yesterday's bond rally was a bet on crude rolling over; today WTI printed $104.32 with oil/gold at a 52-week high and Asia's semiconductor complex broke in Seoul.
summary: The disinflation premise lasted one session. WTI is +2.3% to 104.32, +15.4% on the month and +81.7% year-to-date, sitting 21.0% above its 200-day with z=1.25. Oil/gold jumped 3.5% today, +21.2% on the month, and is now at the 100th percentile of its 52-week range. DBC is in the 96.9th percentile. The 5-year breakeven at 2.47 is turning up, +13bp on the month, and the 30-year mortgage is 7.24% — up 21bp on the month even as the 10-year fell 28bp to 4.98. The inflation composite is -50, still the worst number on the sheet, and the risk regime slipped to -14 from -12. Meanwhile duration got bought hard: IEF +2.4% on the month at acceleration 2.0, TLT acc 1.72, MOVE -12.3% with acceleration -2.23. A two-sigma duration rally against a 15% monthly move in crude is a position, not a forecast.

Overnight the break was in Asia, not in the mega-caps. KOSPI -3.5% at z=-2.27 — the worst single z-score on the board today — now -16.2% on the month and 12.5% below its 200-day, with EWY -13.5% on the month despite being +66.5% YTD. Taiwan -2.5%, Nikkei -2.1% (z=-1.27), Shanghai -1.4% at the 0th percentile. This matters because last week was a semis melt-up: SMH +7.3% on the week, SOXX +8.0%, AMD +11.5%, MU +9.1%, ASML +7.5%. That bounce is now failing — SMH is -7.5% on the month, SOXX -9.4%, SMH/SPY acceleration -1.95, QQQ/SPY acceleration -2.02, and MU -5.0% yesterday. VIX is +7.0% to 18.41 and turning up, the term structure at 0.888 is turning up, SKEW is 151 and +4.5% on the month. Credit still refuses to confirm: HYG/IEF -1.6% on the month at z=-1.27.

What's absorbing the money has not changed, but the composition got more defensive, not less. XLV +2.4% at the 100th percentile with z=1.8 and relative strength +7.1% on the month; LLY +6.6% in a day, +16.0% on the month, 26.3% above its 200-day; IBB at the 100th percentile. LMT is the largest positive score anywhere on the sheet — z=3.35, acceleration 3.37, +25.6% on the month — while ITA sits at only the 30th percentile and 6.3% below its 200-day. Financials are quietly rebuilding: XLF +5.4% on the month at acceleration 1.63, KIE acc 1.94, JPM acc 0.96. Breadth looks spectacular — RSP/SPY acceleration 2.96, equal-weight at the 95.6th percentile, IWM +2.7% on the week — but SPLV is z=2.06/acc 2.46, USMV at the 97th percentile, MCD acc 2.94, HD acc 2.73, and high-beta/low-vol is -11.4% on the month at z=-1.87. Growth/value is at the 4th percentile of the year. This is rotation into safety, not appetite.

The periphery keeps deteriorating and the dollar headline hides it. DXY -0.4% to 101.64 on EUR +0.4% and GBP +0.7%, but USD/MXN is +1.3% to 18.866, at the 100th percentile of the year with z=1.67, and USD/BRL is +6.1% on the week after EWZ lost 20.8% in five sessions. EM/SPY is -7.6% on the month at z=-1.84. Precious metals are still being liquidated rather than sold: gold -1.2% through 4000 to 3984.6 at the 4.7th percentile, silver -3.3% and -16.1% on the month, platinum -3.8% at the 0th percentile with z=-1.85, GDXJ -12.8% on the month, gold/silver z=2.0. The one clean positive in commodities is copper/gold at the 99.8th percentile — global demand is not collapsing. US machinery is: CAT -21.5% on the month at z=-2.58, XLI relative strength -8.0% over three months, COPX -11.2%, REMX -18.7%.

good.text: Rate volatility keeps compressing: MOVE -12.3% on the month at acceleration -2.23, the whole curve 27-28bp lower on the month, 10y real yield down 28bp to 2.63. Cheap optionality on everything rate-linked.
The median stock is working: equal-weight +5.0% on the month at the 95.6th percentile, RSP/SPY acceleration 2.96 — the highest reading on the board — IWM +2.7% on the week, MDY turning up.

Health care is the new leadership and it is confirmed by fundamentals, not flows alone: XLV at the 100th percentile (+7.8% month, rs +7.1%), LLY +6.6% in a session, IBB at the 100th percentile, UNH +9.6% on the month.
Financials turning up under the surface: XLF +5.4% on the month with relative strength turning up, KRE +4.3%, KIE acceleration 1.94, JPM acceleration 0.96 — a steep curve and no credit event yet.
Energy equities are validating the commodity rather than lagging it: XLE +11.7% on the month at the 96.6th percentile, XOP +11.7%, OIH +8.2% on the week, XOM and CVX both at the 98th percentile.

Asian funding stress is absent even as Asian equities fall: USD/CNY at the 0th percentile of the year (-0.9% month), USD/KRW -1.3% on the month, EM currency basket flat. This is a positioning unwind, not a dollar squeeze.

bad.text: Crude re-accelerated and took the inflation trade with it: WTI +2.3% to 104.32 (+15.4% month, 21% above its 200-day), oil/gold at the 100th percentile, 5y breakeven turning up at 2.47, 30y mortgage stuck at 7.24%.
Asia cracked overnight and it is the semiconductor chain: KOSPI -3.5% at z=-2.27 and -16.2% on the month, Taiwan -2.5%, Nikkei -2.1%, EWY -13.5% on the month after being +66.5% YTD.
Last week's semis bounce is failing: SMH -7.5% and SOXX -9.4% on the month, SMH/SPY acceleration -1.95, QQQ/SPY acceleration -2.02, MU -5.0% and AMD -2.1% in a session.

Volatility is bidding into a defensive tape: VIX +7.0% to 18.41 and turning up, term structure turning up at 0.888, SKEW 151 (+4.5% month), while HYG/IEF is -1.6% on the month at z=-1.27. Credit never confirmed the equal-weight rally.
Mega-cap damage is compounding, not healing: GOOGL -16.7% on the month at z=-2.28, META -15.5% with acceleration -2.72, XLC at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range and -9.2% on the month.

US capex and machinery keep breaking: CAT -21.5% on the month at z=-2.58 and 19.7% below its 200-day, XLI relative strength -8.0% over three months, COPX -11.2%, REMX -18.7%, high-beta/low-vol -11.4% at z=-1.87.

trades.name: Sell the duration rally via TLT puts
trades.line: Short duration: 2-sigma bond rally vs $104 crude
trades.expr: Buy TLT Dec 80 puts funded by selling Dec 86 calls; or short IEF outright, 1.5x notional vs book.
trades.thesis: The 27-28bp monthly rally across the curve was priced off a crude rollover that reversed today. With WTI +15.4% on the month, oil/gold at a 52-week high and the 5y breakeven turning up, the long end is carrying inflation risk it is not being paid for. MOVE at -12.3% on the month makes the options cheap.
trades.trigger: IEF acceleration 2.0 and TLT acceleration 1.72 — a two-sigma duration bid — into WTI 104.32 (+2.3% today) and 30y mortgage at 7.24%, up 21bp on the month while the 10y fell 28bp.
trades.stop: WTI back below 95 or 10y through 4.80 with breakevens falling; that means the disinflation read was right.

trades.name: Own S&P downside while vol is still at the 28th percentile
trades.line: Buy Dec SPY put spreads: VIX 18.4, SKEW 151
trades.expr: Buy Dec SPY 750/700 put spreads; add a small long VIX Dec 22 call strip.
trades.thesis: The index is 5.7% above its 200-day at the 93rd percentile while its leadership is low-vol and staples, the AI complex is -3.1% on the month and credit refuses to confirm. Convexity is the cheapest asset on the sheet.
trades.trigger: VIX +7.0% to 18.41 and turning up with the term structure turning up, SKEW 151 (+4.5% month), HYG/IEF z=-1.27, and KOSPI printing a -2.27 z overnight.
trades.stop: VIX back under 15 with HYG/IEF turning up and SMH/SPY reclaiming its 1-month loss.

trades.name: Long XLE vs short SPY
trades.line: Long XLE / short SPY: crude re-accelerating
trades.expr: Long XLE, short equal notional SPY. Overlay long XOM/CVX if you want single-name beta.
trades.thesis: Energy is the only sector whose relative strength is up on both the 1-month and 3-month windows while the commodity itself is making new highs. If crude stays bid, it is simultaneously a long and a hedge against the inflation leg that breaks the index multiple.
trades.trigger: WTI +2.3% to 104.32 with oil/gold at the 100th percentile; XLE relative strength +10.9% on the month and +12.7% on three months, XOM and CVX both at the 98th percentile, OIH +8.2% on the week.
trades.stop: WTI closes below 95 or XLE relative strength rolls over to flat on the month.
trades.target: XLE 76 and another 8% of relative strength.

trades.name: Short Korea (EWY)
trades.line: Short EWY: z=-2.27 break with +66% YTD still to unwind
trades.expr: Short EWY; or buy Jan EWY 150 puts. Pair with a small long EWT if you want to isolate Korea.
trades.thesis: Korea is the most crowded expression of the AI capex trade in the world and the tape is finally rejecting it. The index is 12.5% below its 200-day but the ETF is still only 0.21% below its own and +66.5% YTD — the unwind has barely started in dollar terms.
trades.trigger: KOSPI -3.5% at z=-2.27, the worst score on the board, -16.2% on the month; EWY -13.5% on the month at z=-1.66 and rolling over; SOXX -9.4% on the month with acceleration -1.49.
trades.stop: EWY reclaims 172 or SMH/SPY turns up through its 1-month high; a won squeeze (USD/KRW under 1310) with equities up also kills it.

trades.name: Long XLV vs short XLK
trades.line: Long XLV / short XLK: 100th pctile vs failing semis
trades.expr: Long XLV, short equal notional XLK. Express the long side with LLY and IBB if you want more torque.
trades.thesis: The money evicted from the AI complex is going into drugs and devices with earnings behind it, not into cash. Health care has the strongest relative-strength profile on the sheet (+7.1% 1m, +8.7% 3m, turning up) against technology whose 1-month relative strength is -3.6% and whose semiconductor core is decelerating.
trades.trigger: XLV +2.4% at z=1.8, 100th percentile, with LLY +6.6% and IBB at the 100th percentile; XLK -1.2% with acceleration -0.82 and SMH -7.5% on the month.
trades.stop: XLK relative strength turns up on a semis re-acceleration, or XLV gives back 5% of relative performance.

trades.name: Long USD/MXN
trades.line: Long USD/MXN: 100th pctile, LatAm contagion widening
trades.expr: Buy USD/MXN spot or 3-month forwards; or buy 3-month USD calls, 19.50 strike.
trades.thesis: Latin American funding is deteriorating fast while the local equity market is still pricing optimism. USD/MXN at the top of its 52-week range with a 1.67 z-score and Brazil's currency up 6.1% in a week is contagion, not idiosyncrasy — and the broad dollar is falling, which makes the peso's weakness a credit signal.
trades.trigger: USD/MXN +1.3% today to 18.866, +4.6% on the month at the 100th percentile, while DXY is -0.4% and EUR is +0.4%; EM/SPY -7.6% on the month at z=-1.84; MXX local index +7.2% on the month — a divergence that usually resolves against the equity.
trades.stop: 18.30 — a clean break back inside the range with USD/BRL stabilizing.

trades.name: Long ITA (defense catch-up to LMT)
trades.line: Long ITA: LMT z=3.35 but ITA only 30th pctile
trades.expr: Buy ITA; or buy Jan ITA 220 calls.
trades.thesis: The single largest positive score on the entire board is a defense prime, yet the sector ETF is below its 200-day and in the bottom third of its 52-week range after a -13.4% three-month relative stretch. That gap closes upward in a tape that wants non-cyclical, non-AI earnings.
trades.trigger: LMT z=3.35 with acceleration 3.37 and +25.6% on the month; ITA +3.2% today with acceleration 1.55 and +4.8% on the week off a 30th-percentile base.
trades.stop: ITA back below 205, or LMT's move reverses by more than a third — that would mark it as a one-stock event.
